question: What is the medical reason for performing Female Genital Mutilation (FGM)?

options.A: Enhancement of fertility during childbearing years
options.C: Prevention of chronic pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: There is no medical justification for the procedure

explanation: You got this! FGM has zero health benefits. It's done purely for cultural or social reasons based on myths, not science. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is FGM considered a human rights violation?

options.A: It is performed without informed consent and harms the body
options.B: It violates international trade and economic agreements
options.C: It guarantees that women will never be able to work
options.D: It is practiced exclusively in urban hospital environments

explanation: Think about it: young girls cannot give valid consent, yet they suffer permanent physical harm. That's why it's a major human rights issue. Keep pushing forward! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which type of FGM involves narrowing the vaginal opening and creating a covering seal?
explanation: Type III is known as infibulation. It involves cutting and repositioning the labia to form a seal, leaving just a tiny opening for urine and periods. You're mastering your clinical terms! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h2)

question: What does Type IV FGM involve?

options.A: Surgical reconstruction of damaged labial tissue
options.B: Pricking, piercing, scraping, or cauterizing the genital area
options.C: Complete removal of the uterus and ovaries

explanation: Type IV is the catch-all category for any other harmful, non-medical tinkering with female genitalia. Every question you answer makes you a sharper nurse! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is a major social reason families continue to practice FGM?

options.B: A direct recommendation by the national medical association
options.C: The prevention of childhood infectious diseases
options.D: Fear of social exclusion and unmarriageability

explanation: Sadly, many families do it because they fear their daughters will be rejected by the community or struggle to find husbands. Understanding this helps you treat patients with empathy. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why is community conversation so important when trying to stop FGM in local Nigerian settings?

options.A: Traditional leaders have no influence over community behavior
options.B: Local laws forbid nurses from ever talking about reproductive health
options.C: The practice is deeply tied to cultural identity and social acceptance
options.D: Economic penalties are the only proven way to change minds

explanation: Because FGM is rooted in deep traditions and social pressure, laws alone aren't enough—we need community-wide education to change hearts and minds. You've got this! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is an immediate physical complication right after FGM?
explanation: Cutting sensitive genital tissue—often with unsterilized tools—frequently leads to heavy bleeding, intense pain, and shock right away. Brilliant effort! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h4)

question: A woman with a history of Type III FGM comes in for labor. What should the nurse watch out for?

options.A: Total absence of uterine contractions throughout the first stage
options.B: Obstructed labor and severe scarring requiring careful evaluation
options.C: Spontaneous healing of the infibulated scar without intervention
options.D: Rapid and completely painless expulsion of the placenta

explanation: That thick scar tissue blocks the normal stretching of the birth canal, often causing obstructed labor that needs careful handling. Clinical nursing in action! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is dyspareunia, a common complaint among FGM survivors?

options.B: Chronic swelling of the lower legs

explanation: Dyspareunia simply means persistent pain during sex, usually resulting from severe scarring and nerve damage. Knowing this helps you support your patients better! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why do many FGM survivors hesitate to speak up about their sexual and mental struggles?

options.A: Psychological symptoms disappear completely after marriage
options.B: Cultural taboos make discussing female sexuality difficult
options.C: Hospitals routinely provide mandatory counseling at birth
options.D: Mental health professionals are legally banned from treating women

explanation: Strict societal taboos around sex and reproductive parts force many women to hide their pain and suffer in silence. As a nurse, your gentle care creates a safe space for them. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h5)

question: What approach matters most when doing a physical assessment on an FGM survivor?

options.A: Insisting that family members stay in the room to answer questions
options.B: Avoiding any visual inspection of the perineal area entirely
options.C: Trauma-informed care that prioritizes patient dignity and consent
options.D: Rushing through the examination to minimize patient embarrassment

explanation: Trauma-informed care builds trust, makes the patient feel safe, and respects her boundaries during sensitive exams. You are becoming a wonderfully compassionate nurse! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a goal of identifying FGM in a clinical setting?

options.A: Protecting younger female siblings from undergoing the practice
options.B: Anticipating and preparing for potential obstetric complications
options.C: Publicly shaming the family in the hospital waiting room
options.D: Providing appropriate referrals for psychological support

explanation: Nurses never shame or punish families! Our job is to provide clinical care, educate, offer support, and protect vulnerable children. Keep up the stellar work! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h6)

question: What does 'deinfibulation' mean when managing FGM complications?

options.A: Routine removal of the ovaries to prevent hormonal imbalances
options.B: A traditional herbal massage used to reduce pelvic inflammation
options.C: The practice of re-sewing the labia tightly after every menstrual cycle
options.D: Surgical opening of the scar tissue seal to restore normal anatomy

explanation: Deinfibulation is simply surgically opening the fused labia (from Type III FGM) so the patient can urinate, menstruate, and give birth safely. Fantastic job learning this! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team needed for comprehensive FGM care?

options.A: Patients refuse to speak to nurses unless a doctor is present
options.B: Surgeons are legally required to manage all aspects of nursing care
options.C: Medical insurance only covers care if multiple specialists sign off
options.D: The physical, psychological, and obstetric needs of survivors are complex

explanation: Because FGM affects physical health, childbirth, and mental health all at once, teamwork among different specialists gives the patient the best care possible. You're doing awesome! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is the main goal of laws like the Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Act regarding FGM?

options.A: To provide financial grants to families who continue the tradition
options.B: To criminalize the practice and penalize those who perform it
options.C: To force hospitals to perform FGM under sterile conditions
options.D: To ban female healthcare workers from treating reproductive issues

explanation: Legal frameworks exist to stop the practice by setting clear criminal penalties for anyone who performs or promotes FGM. You're flying through these! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h8)

question: What is a key advocacy duty for a nurse working to end FGM?

options.A: Keeping quiet about the practice to avoid offending elders
options.B: Educating communities and protecting girls at risk
options.C: Performing modified procedures to satisfy cultural demands safely
options.D: Reporting every adult survivor to the police for prosecution

explanation: Nurses serve as educators and champions by raising awareness and shielding young girls from harm before it happens. Another step closer to clinical excellence! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h8)
